t: You're on William IV Street, which runs from Charing Cross Road in the west to Agar Street in the east, where it meets the Strand with pedestrian-only access. The street is named for William IV, who was King of the United Kingdom and Hanover from 1830 until his death in 1837. He was the third son of George III and came to the throne after his elder brother George IV. He was the last king, and the penultimate monarch, of the House of Hanover in the United Kingdom.
